utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. I am glad to see that no one was blown away during the weekend. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. As far as I have been informed, all the practical problems that asked our attention last Thursday have been solved, at least. Yes, I see nodding from both sides. So we could then continue to examine Witness DP 10. Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Yes, Madam Usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. DP10. You hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see that the protective measures are effective. May I remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you have given at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. With the help of Madam Usher, I will take the liberty of distributing this map. Could it be please placed on the ELMO. In point of fact, it is the same map, the same number with 1, because this is the same section of the map that we saw yesterday. So it is 1766.1 because it is the same type of document. And I will ask -- also ask Madam Usher to...

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The counsel's microphone is not switched on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Will you push the button of your microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course. It is Monday morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. DP10, if you bow you head too much to the ELMO, we have no protective measures on the ELMO. We have on all the cameras but not the ELMO. Apart from that, it takes away the view also from us from the ELMO. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Piletta-Zanin: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Last week you made a point or rather a cross in number " 1" in the western part of this map. And I will be grateful if you do the same thing now, quickly. Take the black marker and indicate with a cross and a number perhaps a finer marker, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be given the other marker. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to indicate with a cross and a number "2," "3," et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we perhaps zoom in slightly on where the marking has been made.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Exactly, but will you encircle those two figures. Please make a circle around them and tell us what is number "2" and what is number "3."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 2 is Zrak company. Number 3 is the electrical engineering school. At least, that is what it was before the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, please tell us, what is it that was in the electric engineering faculty?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A workshop making shells.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how did you learn that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave you names of witnesses last Friday, that is people who lived in Sarajevo at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Very well. But that is what we are talking about, isn't it. Thank you. Witness, now, I would like you to be shown another map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which is P3728. But, Madam Usher, we have made copies of the map, and unfortunately there is a marking on this map, but it is self-explanatory as we shall see. It is our number, 1668 and that tell us about the Prosecution exhibit that I have just indicated 3728, and I would like this map, Madam Registrar, would be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise this place which is indicated on the map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The counsel's microphone is off.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So sorry. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you take the pointer and point at the stadium please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, can you tell us how tall were the walls supporting the -- around the stadium?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ten metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, I would like you now to focus --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In order to follow, I did not know the word you used for the -- what was supporting around the stadium. And I thought I would see it in the English translation. But unfortunately, that does not appear in the translation either.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes. I am so sorry. I am talking about the staircase that is the where the seats are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, will you please focus on point 15 that you can see on the screen. Thank you. Do you see -- do you see that under the diagonal -- up diagonal line right at the number 15 -- no, no, no. I am talking about the upper line, yes. And then proceed to the left. Proceed to the left. Proceed to the left. Now, the line, the line, Witness -- no, this is to the right. Thank you. Further, further. Stop. Stop. And at this particular place, Witness, there is a rectangular bar, rectangle which is under the point. Can you tell us what is this rectangle.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an eight-storey building.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I make it precise for the transcript that the witness has pointed at a rectangle indicating the building crossed by the red diagonal which marks one of the limits of the trajectory. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have just told us that it as eight storeys. I believe I heard you, but I am not sure if it is in the transcript. Yes. Thank you. Witness, now, from what used to be MUP, will you place the pointer on the other side of the triangle. No, no, no. I am talking about the base of the triangle. Very well.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, move to the centre of the base of the triangle.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Thank you. From this point which you have indicated and that is the centre of the -- the middle point of the base of the triangle. According to what you know about the area, is it possible to fire at point number 15 with a firearm? I am talking about direct shots. Yes or no and why?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, will you tell us why, to your knowledge, that is not possible?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not possible because the stadium is too tall and this building, and where the victim was, there were always screens, busses or carpets or something, so that you could never see people here nor could one move there, that is, this point. This point was quite well protected. You couldn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, now I would like you to very quickly --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And can we have on the ELMO photograph 3244. This is a photograph. I can give it directly to Madam Registrar, with your permission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We usually take the original and Madam Registrar will --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question that I will ask you with regard to the photograph you will see on the screen is as follows: The building that you talked to us -- whether the building that you mentioned is the one that is shown on the photograph, that is the first thing; and then to check the number of floors.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the exhibit P3244 has been marked. Is the marking of any relevance for this witness, and would the Prosecution oppose against showing the nonmarked copy to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, if we could just be shown the markings on 3244. The copy we have does not have those markings.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution has no objection to either of those photographs being shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, do you want to show the marked or the unmarked photograph to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think it is better to have a pristine photograph, if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then do you want to tender it because then we have it give it -- no. So the unmarked version is now shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have this image to your right. Does either of these building that we can see here tell us what you have just told us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is this building here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Is this building as tall as the other one that is in the background facing us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Tell us how many floors do you see? How many storeys are there of the building on the left side of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Eight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please count them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Eight storeys and the ground floor, so it is a 9-storey building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This photograph can be removed. And I would like now the witness to be shown another exhibit which is our Exhibit 1767. It is a map of the incident number 10. Mr. President, I will show this witness a colour map. I know that we worked in black and white, but we know these maps very well by now, I believe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise this; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, you have two colours indicating the positions of the lines of the adversaries on this map. The ABiH is light and the ARS is dark, dark green.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For -- to all of us, the ARS cannot be seen well in black and white, but it is north of the dark green.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Insofar as the Serb positions are concerned, are these positions correct, from what you know about them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, why and could you -- why to begin with, and then could you please redraw them, according to what you know.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are not because some structures, some streets are shown as they were in the Serb territory and they never were and I can point at them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I would appreciate it if you could take a marker -- no, you are right, please point with the pointer and then after that, mark your positions.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is -- okay -- right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If we just, yes. So we can follow the witness when pointing at certain streets.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, this line here is okay up to this point. And then it goes -- this is the Strojorad building, and it belonged to the opposite side. And the line went down here to the corner of the stadium. Our positions were here. And then it went back towards the police, the MUP club, and then it went up Ozrenicka Street, here it says Ozrenska. And then it followed Ozrenska Street, so the houses were below the road. That is where the trenches to this intersection to Moravska Street and that was the end of the line to which we can see the city of Sarajevo. And here our line drops down because it goes down and we cannot see Sarajevo. And we move on to Djukica Potok or Lukavica, whichever way. That is how the line went. So it goes to this junction towards Ozrenska and Moravska and this is the last point from which we can see Sarajevo. And from here we drop because this is a hill. We go down and move towards Lukavica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, we have at this point, no indication at what time frame the witness is referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please clarify that, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Could you also try to -- well, marking will be made on the map later on, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you are quite right, Your Honour. In order to save time and this is a portion of the answer for the record, we will ask the witness to confirm. I think he used the term "horizon" in his language when he expressed in B/C/S which I don't see clearly indicated in the transcript. In other words, the ridge line from where it was possible to see and then the part of the line from which it was no longer possible to see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please, Witness, mark once again, precisely the position, the Serb positions along this line.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: So, this is correct, so I don't need to correct this one. I shall proceed from here. This portion here is no longer significant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you, Witness. I should like to ask you to indicate for us 622, 23, on the junction -- yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The point which you have just indicated which corresponds to a junction, are you sure that this point corresponds to the point where your lines ended and why? Why are you sure?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spent three years there, after all. That is the last point, as I said, that was important -- that is important in this context. I mean, this is the last point where we had the vision of Sarajevo. Anything coming after this point would be placed from where we were not able to target Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you indicate with a red circle -- I mean, could you indicate in the red circle which appears on the left side who was deployed in this area at this position throughout the relevant times, I mean throughout the times in respect of which you have some knowledge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Army of BH.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, I should like to show you a different photograph now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P3228 -- 68.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: 3268, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will take the example marked as -- we have a copy of this, Your Honours, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We will take the one marked with 4324, the ERN number, and then 4325. That will be the order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: These are the marked photographs that's what you wanted to show. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have a photograph on your right, Witness. Do you recognise this area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. This is the Krndeljeva Street junction at Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I should like you to ask you to indicate with a pointer the hill that we see in the background, that is the central point.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. You are now indicating the hill. Thank you. This hill, under whose control was it during the conflict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The army of the Federation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Witness, to your knowledge, the point indicated in blue colours slightly to the right of a lamp post --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, very well. You are now indicating. This -- on which territory, on whose territory was it, according to what you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This belonged to the federal area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, there seem to be two circles and it is unclear as to which one the witness was referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness was pointing to the circle in the street next to number "2" Mr. Piletta-Zanin, where I had the feeling that you wanted the witness to point to the circle just above the ridge of the hill. Is that correct? That one? Yes. But he was pointing at the other circle when he answered your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't see the other circle. Let me try again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where is the -- this other circle --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, I see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No, no, no. The witness indicated the right circle, but we can ask him again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, would you please place your pointer on the circle which we find under the horizon, to the right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Leave it there, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will describe it for the record. Thank you. The witness has indicated with his pointer the upper circle which we found on this photograph in the sky lightly to the left in relation to the lamp post.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In response to my question in relation to this you responded this territory was in the hands of the BH Army. My second question in relation to this is during which period of time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I arrived there in October 1992 and I stayed there until the end of the war and the line never changed in this area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should like the witness to be shown a different photograph. This one can be taken away. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution objects. The witness was asked to clarify and simply Mr. Piletta-Zanin restated what the witness testified without putting any question to the witness without seeking a clarification. And also, --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And also in the Prosecution submission, he mischaracterised that evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Could you perhaps -- I have to get the right transcript on my screen. Yes. The clarification was, first of all, to see whether there was any misunderstanding as far as the point indicated by the witness. Could we perhaps first have the last photograph again on the ELMO. Witness, could you again point to the circle just right to the lamp post in the -- approximately on the ridge of the hill.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So that everything is clear in this case all of these points, one, two and three, are located in the federal area. The lines, the separation lines held by the Serbs cannot be seen because of this building. So all of this area was in the hands of the Federation. So it is only somewhere behind this building that the lines of the VRS soldiers began.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand that the whole of the hill visible on this photograph was in the hands of the BiH. That is your testimony, that is clear.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, please proceed. Mr. Mundis

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: For the record, Mr. President, when the witness referred to the building, that should be indicated as the large white building towards the left centre of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That is what he pointed at. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the other one, consequently.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, on the basis of the other photograph --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we can have this one as well, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, would you please indicate on this photograph at the large white facade that you can see on the right side of the photograph--

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. The witness is now indicating the building with the blind facade. When I said the building with the blind facade, I was meaning -- I meant the one which has no windows on it. This facade, witness, how far does it stretch compared to the street which we can see in the centre of this photograph which is therefore, parallel with respect to the building in question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This building is also 9 floors tall, approximately, and it stretches westward from the south. This white side of the building is facing the Serb positions on the hill located towards Vraca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, what we need to know is how far into the street does this facade stretch? In other words, what is the distance between this building and the hill? How far does it go with respect to the street? Are there any other buildings of this height in this area or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a very close shot. There are other buildings here as well. This is a close up. If the photograph had been taken from afar, you would have seen other buildings as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please use your pointer and indicate the -- slightly more to the left please -- a point that we can see on this photograph, a marking that we can see on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. That is the one that I was referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness is now referring to a blue colour point which indicates approximately the scene of the incident.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, the point that you have just indicated, to your knowledge, and in light of the terrain in particular the building on the right side was it accessible to shots coming from the left, from the Serb-held area that you indicated a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not far from this point here southward, in the vicinity of these buildings, these houses here, there used to be a relatively tall building where the command of the Federation army was located. We used to refer to this place as taxi's club and this was some kind of protection, some kind of shelter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me stop you, Witness, my question was a purely technical one. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. From the positions you held and which you have shown us a moment ago, was it technically possible to target directly to scene of the incident that you are now indicating with the pointer? Was it possible to target this spot with direct shots; yes or no and why? In light, of course, of the nature of the terrain in the area, and the placement of buildings in question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was not possible because we couldn't see the spot for this building. We could see just the angle of this building. And, again, with respect to Ozrenska Street, our positions were somewhat lower.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you telling us, Witness, that it was not possible to see the spot and was it possible to target the scene of the incident; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was not possible. Because we would have shot only at this building, at this side of the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, you spoke about a military facility in the area. Can you describe for us briefly what it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have indicated, you cannot properly see the spot on this photograph. But in this area here, there used to be a building before the war which we referred to as taxi driver's club. The location became the command of the people who held the lines -- the positions here in this area in Hrasno. So this rather large building was their command. They had protected themselves very well. You couldn't see the exact location because of the houses around this vicinity.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I shall stop you because my learned colleague seems to have an objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, we previously objected on the grounds that is we didn't have clarification with respect to what time frame. We renew that objection with respect to the previous questions but also with respect to this line of questioning specifically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, would you please take this into consideration when continuing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the witness has just indicated a location which we were ignorant of and it seems to be a command. We didn't know that. If we establish that there were such locations all over Sarajevo, I know that the Prosecution is opposed to that, and I can simply take note of that. But the witness should indicate to us, nevertheless, what period of time he was talking about.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe I was clear enough. Before I started my testimony about this, I indicated that I was deployed ever since October 1992 until the end of the war. So I was referring to the period of time between end of 1992 and 1995. That entire period of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question is whether during that entire period of time this building did exist, as you called it, the driver's club. Yes. During the entire period of time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Please proceed. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, may I just ask you, how much time was scheduled for this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Two hours without breaks, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Until now, you took two hours and ten minutes, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Without interruptions, you mean?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Normal interruptions are included in the time, as you know, and there were no -- there were no interruptions such that would cause us to change the account of time. Perhaps this is the moment to say that the Chamber will be relatively strict on this. We have had some --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... use your time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will need only a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you know, and this is a general question, if in the city of Sarajevo, according to your knowledge, there was a significant number, yes or no, of targets, military targets? I am referring to the area controlled by the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us once again, generally speaking, if these military targets - I am referring to the command posts - were usually located on higher floors or lower floors of the building, according to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, mostly they were located on ground floor, that's where they were safe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if these military targets were located in the buildings that in the past had been civilian buildings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What type of buildings would that have been, as an example?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well I mentioned the taxi driver's club. And then at Marijn Dvor they were located at the former Assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina, at the Holiday Inn hotel. I believe this is enough.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What can you tell us about residential buildings in this context?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have indicated, they were usually located in the basements of those buildings or on the ground floor of such buildings, which were still inhabited by civilians, by regular residents. So they could also become victims of potential attacks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I don't think I have already -- I have asked that question but do you know if there was at Grbavica the protection communication lines which enabled the civilians to move around?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to the protection against sniper shooting? Are you referring to the screens?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, yes, if you have used the word "screen," yes, I was referring to that as well.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were many such types of protection, wherever there was a risk of sniper fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Are you ready to cross-examine the witness, Mr. Mundis?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have to interrupt once again. Mr. Mundis, I apologise for that. The record does not indicate properly my question which is important, as most of my questions. I was referring to the person by the name of Dragonov. I asked if you knew what a Dragonov was and the witness said he didn't. On page 29, we see that there is nothing in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I was listening to the French channel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And at least I heard Mr. Piletta-Zanin ask what whether the witness knew what a Dragonov was. And although I could not hear his answer in his own language, your answer was "no"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For the transcript --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- It is clarified now. Mr. Mundis, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I would ask first with the assistance of the usher that the witness be shown Defence Exhibit 1767, please. Cross-examined by Mr. Mundis:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DP10, in response to a question from the Judge on Wednesday, you told us that your platoon was at different locations along the confrontation line during the time period that you were there, that is, from October 1992 through 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the area of Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the black line that you have marked on 1767 reflects the confrontation lines that your unit operated along?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would ask you to take a blue thin-lined marker. Can you tell us approximately where on the line your platoon was located in October 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you could please place the letter "O" and the numbers "92" next to that dot, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During November 1992, where was your platoon located? If you could place an "N92" next to that, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In December 1992, where was your platoon located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During 1993, did your platoon also operate along this confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From 1992 until 1995, the entire period of time. We would spend 15 days here, 15 here and then 15 there. We were rotated. Excuse me, my company consisted of three platoons and we took turns all the time until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able, as a result of this rotation, were you able to come to an understanding of the unique facets at each point along that confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our responsibility was always the same.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness come closer to the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, would the witness -- the microphone of the witness come closer to him or the witness closer to the microphone. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Our responsibility along all the lines --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like some precision. What does "unique facets" mean precisely. It is not quite clear, at least to the Defence. It is not clear what is meant. Can it be made more precise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For example, Witness DP10, during November 1992, at the spot that you have marked on the map D1767, can you tell us about any trench lines, fortification lines, or other unique situations concerning the front line at that point during the month of November 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were four skyscrapers along the Miljacka. And then you see many buildings are not shown here. Because there were 60.000 inhabitants in Grbavica before the war, but not all these buildings are shown here. On this map there aren't any buildings. So here there are buildings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am asking you, Witness, please, specifically about the point on the line that you have marked where you platoon was located in November 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is where a trench was, a fortification.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, perhaps there is a problem because I believe to have understood in the Serb interpretation the precise word -- the word that should have been used in the Serbian was "ceta," that is, company. But if he means whether he means company or whether he means something else and the witness explains this perhaps he will be able to answer better. The problem has to do with the Serb -- Serbian interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We would check that later on. But the question now was about the position where the witness was stationed in November 1992. He indicated the spot he marked on the map. Could you answer the question in respect of that part.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] N92 is marked here. We had a trench here. Is there anything else I should say?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: DP10, how many men were in your platoon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fifteen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you testified on Wednesday --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just to resolve this misunderstanding, perhaps the witness should be asked whether he was the commander of a platoon or of a company, in view of his answers so far, to avoid creating a misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were you a platoon commander or were you a company commander at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was asked that question on Friday and I said I was a platoon commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, although it was not on Friday. That is my recollection as well. Please proceed, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before the holidays. Before the holidays.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DP10, did you remain a platoon commander from October 1992 through the end of 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that entire time period, did your platoon remain at a strength of approximately 15 men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it depends. Some would leave; some would flee the war; some come. So it was also more or less 15 people plus/minus. Sometimes there were 15; sometimes there were 14. You know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You always testified on Wednesday that you didn't hold any particular rank, other than being the functional title of platoon commander; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that remained the case throughout the period from 1992 through 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you told us a few moments ago that there were three platoons in you company; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Each of these platoons also had approximately 15 men, give or take, during the time period in question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: More or less.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Other than these three platoons, did the company that you were assigned to have any other units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: With a part of infantry units, I don't know whether I get -- but I was with the mechanised armoured battalion, which means I had APCs at my disposal, and I ran them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many APCs did you or did you as the platoon commander have control over during this period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three. Three -- I am talking about my platoon -- three APCs. That is company nine, the company had nine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did these three APCs remain fully operational during the time period from 1992 through 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time periods that your platoon was along the confrontation line did you and your platoon soldiers remain in the APCs or did you assume positions in buildings or trenches?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Next to the APCs, our chief role was to support infantry lines pulling out the wounded, the killed, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would ask that we go into closed session for a few questions, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will turn into closed session. Private session and closed session is the same in this courtroom, so both of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is confirmed on my screen. Please proceed, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DP10, what was the approximate length along the confrontation line that your platoon was responsible for at any given time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: 2.000 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me see if I understand you correctly, Witness. The 15 men in your platoon were responsible for 2.000 metres along the length of the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said we supported the lines. We had infantry lines, that is infantry soldiers who were in the trenches. And we were next to the APCs and in case of the attack of the enemy units we would support then. In case of fatalities, we reacted then, our wounded. So we were not strictly tied to the trenches. At the invitation of our comrades from - what do you call it - the lines, those who were on the lines, it was only then that we would start action. We were not strictly tied to the trench on the front line. And others provided the guard service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you testified on Wednesday about instructions from your superiors not to open fire on civilians. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, I remember it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you testified that you were given those instructions on a daily basis; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How would you characterise the chain of command within from your brigade commander down to yourself as the platoon commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From my post using telephone, but it wasn't far. So I could also walk there. So first I would turn to my immediate commander who was the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. company commander and then to the battalion commander and then on from brigade and then on to the General Staff, that is, from the lower echelons to the upper. That is how we received our orders and that is how we reported about the tasks accomplished.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you characterise the chain of command as one that was very ridged or was there a great degree of latitude given to you as a platoon commander to interpret the orders that you received?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our orders were always - and I as a platoon commander - to be strict, to take care that the soldiers do not wander around the lines or do something illicit, not to fire unnecessarily, not to fire at what they should not fire at. We had a very correct and very strict command. And a very disciplined one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say disciplined, do I assume from that that when you gave an order to your platoon that that order would be carried out?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness DP10, I see you nodding but your answer would be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The previous one?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps I was too early. But I saw you nodding in the affirmative, which is difficult for the interpreters to translate. I am not sure whether the question as a whole was already translated to you. So the last question was whether Mr. Mundis can assume that when you gave an order to your platoon, that the order would be carried out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I could not issue any orders on my own account. I always had to consult with my superiors. So that I was never the one who issued such orders except in case of an attack of the Bosniak side. Then, of course, I defended myself with all the means at my disposal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question was: When you gave an order -- whether you received it from someone else is a different question, but when you gave an order whether your men would carry out that order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well I was, I commanded and they were subordinated to me. They had to do it

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question is whether they did.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Similarly, Witness DP10, when you received an order from your company commander, you carried out that order; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the company commander carried out the orders of the battalion commander; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the battalion commander carried out the orders of the brigade commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All the way up, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to take it to its logical conclusion, the brigade commander followed the orders of the corps commander; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, during the time period from September --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, Mr. President, the Defence objects to this line of questioning. Because it is highly subtle. You asked a question because you wanted to know if the soldiers of the witness's platoon obeyed his orders. And now one proceeds with the same kind of questions. But this witness has no way of knowing whether a colonel or who was responsible for the brigade obeyed the orders of his superior or not. He can only make conjectures, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether he could know or not is just as hypothetical as you suggest the answers of the witness are. On the other hand, Mr. Mundis, of course, the Chamber would certainly be assisted if we would have the source of knowledge of the witness in this respect. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, your objection contains comments as well. If you are objecting, and if you think you couldn't do it without commenting on the answer of the witness you should suggest to the Chamber that we find another solution and we will certainly follow you. But I hope you will keep this in mind. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DP10, during the time that you were a platoon commander from September 1992 through August 1994, did you ever have an occasion to report any of your platoon members for failure to follow an order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have any such cases.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DP10, in the period from September 1992 through August of 1994, are you aware of any incidents where any members of your company were reported or disciplined for failing to follow an order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no such instances. No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: DP10, in the period from September 1992 through August 1994, were you aware of any instances where anyone in your battalion was disciplined or reported for failing to follow an order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, are you aware of anyone in your brigade being disciplined or reported for failing to follow an order during the period September 1992 through August 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the same period, that is, September 1992 through August 1994, are you aware of anyone in the corps being disciplined for failing to follow an order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't that well informed, believe me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I am about to move into another line of questioning and perhaps this would be a good time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then we will perhaps have a break. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, may I just address you on one issue just in order to give you some guidance. The objection you just made could have been made also in wording such as that you would object and that you would have said that it would have been proper to clarify the source of knowledge of the witness in respect of the last two or three questions. That would have been the proper way of doing it. It would have been perfectly clear, both to the Chamber and to the Prosecution, and it gives no comment on the answers. Because part of your objection was what the witness knew or did not know, and that is just speculative, although perhaps probable, but I think you should not comment in such a way on the answers of the witness while being cross-examined by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will have a break until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, I would that the witness be shown the map which has been marked D1767, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I would like you, if you are able to do so, on the map that is before you, to mark please the location of your brigade's headquarters using a blue pen.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You cannot see it here. It is outside the map. I cannot find it here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you say earlier this morning that on occasion you were able to walk to your brigade headquarters from the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Taking the confrontation line at the point where it intersects the MUP building, do you see that on the map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please place a blue X on that location.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please draw an arrow in the general direction of your brigade headquarters from that blue X.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And approximately how far from the blue X was it to your brigade headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: 300 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall the address or the location of which building your brigade headquarters was located in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was at the junction with Zagrebacka Street, where Bana Surbata Street meets Zagrebacka Street and the location was called Aleksandrija. It was a restaurant which was located in this building which was a high-rise building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see the location on map D1767 where your battalion headquarters were located.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You cannot see it on this map. My battalion command was located at Petrovacka Street in the middle of Bana Surbata Street as you climb down from Vraca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please draw an arrow again from the blue X in the direction of your battalion headquarters.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the direction where the command was located. And the company command was located here, whereas the battalion command was located in this area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis, would it assist to use map D1766?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We can try that, Mr. President. If the witness can be shown D1766.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The company command was located here number one. The battalion command or the headquarters was located here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you have marked that with a number "2" for the battalion headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Company headquarters number one, and battalion headquarters number two. So this here is the junction with Zagrebacka Street where the company had orders where this used to be Petrovacka Street and this is where battalion headquarters were located and this street here going down is Bana Surbata.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In order to avoid whatever confusion there is already, another number one on the map which is next to a cross which is Kranjceviceva, which is north of the river Miljacka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you see on this map where the brigade, where your brigade headquarters was located?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in order to be sure that there will be no confusion later on, a blue colour pen I think would be necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the witness -- I looked when the pen was given to him. It had the appearance of blue. Is that correct? Yes. Blue is used, but it might not be that clear on the ELMO scree. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, Witness DP10, if you see on this map before you, D1766, the location where your brigade's headquarters was located, could you please mark that with a circle and a number "3" using the blue pen.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You cannot see the brigade's headquarters. It was located in Lukavica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's fine, Witness, if it is not on the map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here, approximately, in this area, at Lukavica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please mark that with a circle and the number "3" using the blue pen.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is just an approximation. I would need some more space here in this direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's fine, Witness. Was the brigade headquarters located in the same building at Lukavica Barracks as the corps headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We didn't hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I heard -- what I heard was "Na," is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask that the witness now be shown the photograph marked P3244, the photo bearing the number "1A". And while that is being done --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, was the brigade headquarters located at the Lukavica Barracks throughout the period of September 1992 through August 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Not at the barracks, but behind the barracks. But it was part of the barracks, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness has just answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it was not the testimony of the witness that it was in the barracks, but just that it was Lukavica, but he corrected it now. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Can I have a clarification, please on the exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The marked or the unmarked?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The unmarked, please. Also if Madam Registrar could provide the Prosecution with P3278 -- sorry -- 3728, the large bundle of maps, that would be very helpful, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I would ask you to look immediately to the right of the individual standing in the centre of this photograph. Do you see a structure just above his stomach in that photograph? Can you please point to what I am referring to with the pointer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is the stadium; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The stands of the stadium.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And immediately above that and slightly to the left, right in front of that gentleman's chest, you can see the lights of the stadium; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, in the centre of that photograph, there is a small tree. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And behind the tree what appears to be a large white building. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That building is the MUP building, is it not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That photograph can be returned to the Registrar and if I can ask that the witness be shown -- excuse me -- P3268, the photograph marked number "2."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you testified earlier about this intersection. Do you recall what intersection that is depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kranjceviceva Street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This would be the view that you would have had from the SRK lines between September 1992 and August 1994, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is where the defence line of the Bosniak army were located and we were up there, here, in the hills. The Serb forces were deployed on the hill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you see this intersection from your location, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we couldn't. Here in the vicinity was the headquarters of the Bosniak units and the second reason -- I mean, as I said, this was the first line of the Bosniak forces. And this whole street was covered with screens, buses and other vehicles which completely obstructed the view from our side of this junction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, is it your testimony that you could or could not see this junction from the location where your platoon was located from September 1992 through August 1994?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the question needs more precision because the witness has indicated that his platoon would be rotated every two weeks, and that it was deployed along a 2.000 metre long line. I think that my colleague should be more precise in his question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The positions are not that clear if the platoon covered two kilometres of confrontation line, Mr. Mundis. Would you --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I will withdraw that question, Mr. President, and move on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, at any time between September 1992 and August 1994, did you conduct any type of reconnaissance mission into the territory controlled by the Federation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you testified earlier today that there were ABiH headquarters positions located in the ground floors of buildings, you did not have any first-hand knowledge of that situation, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I indicated, we learned this from the people who had left Sarajevo during the war, Croats and Serbs who had managed to leave the town. The bridge, these people could also testify to these circumstances. They were in the relevant area in 1992 and 1993, and managed to escape across these lines, some of which were held by the HVO and reached our area, and remained later on with our army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the fact is that you personally did not see any of these headquarters locations; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw them from -- from the air, from bird's eye view. I don't know how to put it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You saw these locations from positions controlled by the SRK forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, with your leave, Mr. Ierace has a few questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Might I have access to Exhibit P3728. Just while that is being done --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I have it here, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. That can be returned. Cross-examined by Mr. Ierace:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you marked on a map the forward positions, as I understand it, of the Sarajevo Brigade during the time that you served in that brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what month in what year did you commence to serve in that brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 6th of October, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the map --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like us to be as precise as possible. The witness did not indicate on the map the positions of the Sarajevo Brigade. What he indicated was the position that he knew about concerning his battalion. He even stopped at one point and he said that, beyond this point, this is not significant, this is not important. I would like us to -- all to bear this in mind for all future references.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, although the witness answered the question, I take it that he understood that it related to his earlier answers. But the next question was not related any more to confrontation lines, so please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that map you indicated that the forward positions included one corner of the football stadium; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the -- where were the forward positions of the army of the Presidency in relation to the stadium?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the Loris building through the side stadium. There is the main stadium and the auxiliary playground all the way to Mrkevic Street and further on towards Vraca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The stadium was the subject of a number of --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The auxiliary playground, I mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the territory of the stadium, there were a number of battles; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the battles were almost a daily occurrence. And there would be shooting almost every day in this area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I am suggesting to you is that at various times there were attempts by one side or the other to control the territory of the stadium.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. The federal soldiers attacked our positions almost on a daily basis. But they wanted to get hold of our positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I suggest to you that up until August 1994, the most of the stadium that was ever held by the army of the Presidency was one corner.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That one corner was held by the VRS army. The remainder of the area was a kind of no-man's land. Their line, including the trenches, ran across the auxiliary pitch, together with the lawn. So this was the area between the Muslim soldiers and the Serb soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, might the witness be shown Defence Exhibit 1767, and could that please be placed on the ELMO so that we can see the stadium.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, would you please point to the auxiliary pitch.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see it here. This is where the line went, and this is where the pitch is located. And it went right across the pitch.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For the benefit of the transcript, the witness points to an area on the map on which is written "athletic field" to the left of the stadium.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you see a light green line that passes through the athletic's field on the map, and perhaps you could point to it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that that was the forward position of the army of the Presidency at that point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I fully agree with you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, may I ask you to invite the witness to mark the athletic field. Because on our copies, you can't read these words so we will have difficulties in finding it at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please take a fine point blue pen and place a circle around the athletics field, what you called the auxiliary pitch?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks] Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I think you have drawn a square but that is okay. Now, when were you first approached by anyone from the team representing the accused, be it an investigator or a lawyer or anyone else who you understood to be a representative of that team or member of that team?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two days prior to my departure to The Hague.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had no contact before then with any member of the Defence team; is that the case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never. I didn't know those people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you saying that the first contact was within the last two weeks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I can be precise. It was on the 10th of this month, on the 10th of October.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 10th of October --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any idea how it is that your name appeared -- and I will not repeat your name, I will not state it -- that your name appeared on a list of witnesses to be called by the Defence, that list dating from August? Do you know how that could be?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know Mr. Radovic, he was the one who contacted me, Mr. Vojo Radovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But no one asked you if you would be a witness in this case at any stage before the 10th of October; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Vojo Radovic contacted me and since he knew which unit I belonged to, we knew each other from before and he knew that I would be in a position to testify about these things. I had seen Vojo Radovic prior to the 10th of October.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did Mr. Vojo Radovic first contact you in relation to this trial?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometime in midsummer. I don't remember the date. This summer, I mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "sometime in midsummer" could it have been earlier than June 2002?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, thereabouts. June, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace. Are there any questions arising from the cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. If the Prosecution has no further questions, then we would like to ask some.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps we first --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Give an opportunity to the Judges to ask additional questions so that if this would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps you start. If the questions of the Judges would raise any new issue, then of course an opportunity will be given to you. Re-examined by Mr. Piletta-Zanin:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you were asked about instructions that you received or orders that you received and also whether you reported to the company commander, then the battalion commander, the brigade commander and so on and so forth. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I did that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Now, my question with regard to the instructions that you received not to target civilians, is it correct that it went through the same chain of command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the same. The same from the company commander up the ladder.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A moment ago you mentioned the name of the company commander. Am I to understand that therefore, the orders not to target civilians went straight up in a straight line and therefore would be traced to General Galic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, I would like you to be shown now a map -- no, I think it is still on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. The other map, please. The one that we saw a while ago relating to incident number 15 with the red triangle marked. Mr. President, the series of questions that I will ask now arise from questions asked by the Prosecution regarding the presence of MUP. And I would like to have a map or rather a liner to this witness, if possible. If not, we shall try to make do with something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You want a liner -- it is not quite clear to me --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A ruler. A ruler, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you like to have one specific with centimetres on it or --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President. Something to enable the witness to draw a straight line. Perhaps a notebook or something hard enough.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this do?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that the pointer could not do because that is not straight. But if the back of the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The counsel's microphone is off.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this will do. May I move on, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I want you to do the following: You identified point 15 on the map. And I would like you now to draw a straight line - wait, wait, wait - in the direction to the triangle base, but leaving outside the first building. No. No. Put this piece of cardboard down. No, no, no, no. I want us to see the upper part of the triangle.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's it. Perfect. Perfect. Now, draw a line from this point -- no, wait. Wait. As close as possible to the lower left angle, more down, down, further down. Witness -- no, wait. No. Witness, move the ruler to point 15.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
